title: Green Freekeh with Herbs and Toasted Almonds
summary: Boiled whole freekeh tossed warm with a lemon and olive oil dressing, softened red onion, parsley and mint, topped with toasted almonds.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, for the cooking water
fine sea salt or table salt
mint leaves, chopped, plus a few whole leaves

steps.title: Boil the freekeh
steps.text: Bring the 2500 ml water and the cooking salt to the boil, add the freekeh and simmer uncovered for 30-45 min, until tender but still chewy. Cracked freekeh only takes about 20 min, so taste early if that is what you have. Drain well.

steps.title: Toast the almonds
steps.text: Meanwhile, stir the almonds in the dry frying pan over medium-low heat for 5-7 min. Break one in half: it should be lightly golden inside and smell fragrant. Spread them on a plate so they stop cooking.

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Drop the diced onion into the bowl of iced water for 10 min, then drain well. The cold water draws out the harsh sulphur compounds, leaving the onion crisp and mild.

steps.title: Dress while warm
steps.text: Whisk the oil, lemon juice, 0.5 tsp salt and pepper together in the large mixing bowl. Add the warm freekeh, onion, parsley and chopped mint and toss; warm grains soak up the dressing more readily.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Taste and adjust, then pile into a serving bowl. Finish with the whole almonds and mint leaves, and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Pick over the freekeh before rinsing; it can contain small stones or husks.
Undercooking is a common mistake; give whole freekeh the full time until no hard core remains.
Add the almonds just before serving so they stay crunchy.
It holds up well, making it a good packed lunch.
storage: Refrigerate the dressed freekeh covered up to 3 days; keep the almonds separate to stay crisp. Serve cold or at room temperature. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
